decisions.reason: Because the service moved from a mere mention in 2023 to its own page in 2024, management is publicly and visibly more committed and will likely justify continued support by treating any weak uptake as temporary.

This framework appears less strongly committed than the others because it is still only mentioned rather than featured, but as a 2023 launch in a GIS-focused software firm it still benefits from prior development effort and strategic fit, making continuation more likely than withdrawal.

The firm has made the identity service highly visible with a launch statement and a dedicated page, so escalation of commitment and its close link to the firm's GeoIT direction make dropping it within a year unlikely.

As a 2024 launch with its own page, the workshop carries fresh public commitment and low-cost service logic, so management is likely to keep it on offer for at least another year while attributing any disappointing demand to normal market-building time.
